t: The Treaty of Cahuenga was signed, informally ending the fighting of the Mexican–American War in California.
Mexican–American War: The United States Army used artillery to repulse the much larger Mexican army at the Battle of Buena Vista near Saltillo.
Mexican–American War: The Siege of Veracruz began, the first large-scale amphibious assault conducted by United States military forces.
Birkenhead Park, generally acknowledged as the world's first publicly funded civic park, opened in Birkenhead, England.
Prince Afonso died at the age of two, leaving his father Pedro II, the last emperor of Brazil, without a male heir.
Up to ten people died in a riot between Catholics and members of the Orange Order in Woodstock, New Brunswick.
Brigham Young led the first group of Mormon pioneers into the Salt Lake Valley of Utah, at the time a part of Mexico.
